observations.text: SP, due to an incomplete instrument cross-check at the entry to the confidence maneuvers, did not establish the briefed entry airspeed and heading before initiating the aileron roll, and the IP directed the entry parameters and assisted on the controls through the wingover recovery. Rollout was completed 400 feet below entry altitude and 15 degrees off the entry heading, with no unusual attitude allowed to develop. Performance met the standard required at this stage but was marginal; independent setting of entry parameters and unassisted recovery are expected to improve over the next sorties.

SP flew the aileron roll and the wingover using instruments in accordance with the standard procedures of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, with the IP limited to verbal prompts on the entry airspeed. Deviations at rollout reached 300 feet in altitude and 10 degrees in heading, recognized and corrected after the prompt, and no unusual attitude developed. Control of the A/C remained continuous through both maneuvers. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP entered and completed both confidence maneuvers on instruments without IP's intervention, maintaining smooth and continuous control of the A/C. Minor errors were confined to 200 feet in altitude, 15 KIAS at rollout and 7 degrees in heading, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the aileron roll and the wingover on instruments accurately and promptly, according to standard procedures and without IP's intervention. Entry and recovery parameters were held within 100 feet in altitude, 6 KIAS and 4 degrees in heading, and the A/C was at no point brought to an unusual attitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional precision on both confidence maneuvers flown on instruments, with an unbroken cross-check through the roll and the wingover. Recovery parameters were regained within 50 feet in altitude, 3 KIAS and 2 degrees in heading, with control inputs smooth and continuous at every stage. Performance exceeded the level desired for this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient nose-high pitch attitude and low entry airspeed before the aileron roll, did not execute the maneuver according to the standard procedures reported in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, allowing the roll rate to decay through the inverted segment. The A/C was brought to a nose-low unusual attitude and the IP intervened on the controls to recover it, with 450 feet of altitude lost and airspeed 25 KIAS above the entry value. Review of the confidence maneuver entry parameters is required before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments during the wingover, did not maintain constant, smooth and continuous control of the A/C through the descending half of the maneuver. The IP directed the recovery and executed part of it, with the A/C 400 feet below entry altitude, 25 KIAS fast and 15 degrees off the entry heading at rollout. Deliberate transition to the attitude indicator at the first sign of a perception conflict is to be practiced.

SP flew both confidence maneuvers on instruments to the standard required for this stage, completing the wingover only after the IP's verbal prompt on the recovery pitch attitude. Deviations at rollout reached 300 feet in altitude and 10 degrees in heading, recognized and corrected with delay, and no unusual attitude developed. Marginal performance for the Training Section; earlier recognition of the recovery point without prompting is expected to improve.

SP executed the aileron roll and the wingover on instruments without IP's intervention, keeping control of the A/C smooth and continuous. Errors were minor and confined to 180 feet in altitude, 14 KIAS and 6 degrees in heading, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knows and executes the confidence maneuvers according to standard procedures, entering and recovering both the aileron roll and the wingover on instruments with accuracy and speed. Parameters were contained within 120 feet in altitude, 8 KIAS and 4 degrees in heading, without IP's intervention and without any unusual attitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional precision and a well-developed instrument cross-check on both confidence maneuvers, flying entry and recovery to the Techniques and Procedures Manual standard on the first attempt. Deviations were negligible, within 50 feet in altitude, 2 KIAS and 2 degrees in heading, and control of the A/C was constant and smooth throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to uncoordinated rudder application through the vertical segment of the wingover, did not keep the maneuver within the standard procedures of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, allowing the nose to slice below the horizon at the top. The IP took the controls to recover the A/C from the resulting unusual attitude, with 500 feet of altitude lost and airspeed 30 KIAS above the entry value at rollout. Further practice of the wingover entry and of pitch-rate control is required.

SP, due to a startle response at the onset of the rapid roll rate, did not complete the aileron roll without assistance, releasing back pressure and stopping the roll in the inverted attitude. The IP directed the recovery and executed part of it, with the A/C 450 feet low and 20 degrees off the entry heading on rollout. Familiarization with the roll rate and with the memorised recovery sequence is required before the maneuver is repeated.

SP, due to a delayed check of the entry airspeed before the aileron roll, did not initiate the maneuver at the briefed parameters and did not recognize the developing altitude loss until prompted. Following the IP's verbal instructions the roll was completed, with deviations at the limit of 300 feet in altitude, 20 KIAS and 10 degrees in heading, corrected with delay and without control intervention by the IP.

SP, due to attention captured by the attitude indicator alone while the rest of the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not cross-check altitude and heading during the wingover and did not recognize the deviation as it built. The maneuver was completed after the IP's verbal prompts, with rollout 300 feet below entry altitude and 10 degrees off the entry heading, corrected with delay. A cross-check that includes altitude, airspeed and heading through the maneuver is expected.

SP executed both confidence maneuvers on instruments within the desired standards and without IP's intervention; however, the entry heading was regained twice with an overshoot before settling. Deviations remained at 190 feet in altitude, 13 KIAS and 7 degrees in heading, recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the recovery roll-out is expected to improve.

SP knows and executes the confidence maneuvers flawlessly on instruments, according to standard procedures and without IP's intervention, with accuracy and speed at both entry and recovery. Parameters were held within 110 feet in altitude, 7 KIAS and 3 degrees in heading, and at no point was the A/C brought to an unusual attitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the aileron roll and the wingover on instruments with exceptional precision, maintaining constant, smooth and continuous control of the A/C and an uninterrupted cross-check throughout. Recovery was completed with negligible deviations, within 40 feet in altitude, 2 KIAS and 1 degree in heading, on the entry heading and at the entry altitude. Performance was above the level desired for this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.
